name: COPD Pulmonary Rehabilitation
summary: Exercise training, breathing strategies, education and self-management form the core of pulmonary rehabilitation, with oxygen and medical therapies coordinated with the treating team.

looksLike: Exacerbation history and inhaler technique in multidisciplinary care
redFlags: Severe resting hypoxemia outside prescribed parameters
firstSteps: Record dyspnea, SpO2, heart rate, 6MWT/sit-to-stand and exacerbation history.
Review oxygen prescription and medical restrictions.
Teach pacing and breathing control during exertion.

assess: Exacerbation history and inhaler technique in multidisciplinary care

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Exercise training is the core intervention; dyspnea is monitored and managed rather than avoided completely.
do: Record dyspnea, SpO2, heart rate, 6MWT/sit-to-stand and exacerbation history.
Review oxygen prescription and medical restrictions.
Teach pacing and breathing control during exertion.
Assess: SpO2 and heart rate response

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Monitor oxygen saturation and cardiovascular response according to medical status.
do: Inspiratory muscle training in selected patients
dose: Aerobic: interval or continuous training, often 20–40 minutes total, 3–5 days/week as tolerated.
Strength: 2–3 sets × 6–15 reps for major muscle groups, 2–3 days/week.
Inspiratory muscle training only in selected patients with appropriate assessment.
moveOn: Increase duration before intensity in very deconditioned patients
Progress resistance and walking speed while monitoring symptoms and oxygenation

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Airway clearance is indicated when secretion retention exists, not simply because the diagnosis is COPD.
when: Increase duration before intensity in very deconditioned patients
Progress resistance and walking speed while monitoring symptoms and oxygenation
dose: Increase duration first in very deconditioned patients.
Progress resistance and walking speed while monitoring SpO2, dyspnea and recovery.
Use interval training when continuous exercise is not tolerated.
